metadata.title: Praxis Essential Capabilities — cross-domain adult foundation
metadata.source: Custom synthesis; see essential_capabilities_v1.md for references, limits, and assessment proposal.
metadata.notes: Jurisdiction-neutral working seed, not an official standards framework or credential policy. Estimated hours are orientation/practice estimates, not mastery guarantees. Demonstrations are embedded in node descriptions. No formal standards alignment is claimed.

nodes.title: Separate observation, interpretation, and assumption
nodes.description: Capability: distinguish what was directly observed, what was inferred, which assumptions connect them, and what remains unknown. Demonstration: annotate a short case into observations, interpretations, assumptions, and open questions; revise the annotation when new evidence is supplied.

nodes.title: Evaluate sources and trace information provenance
nodes.description: Capability: assess who produced a claim, when and why it was produced, what evidence supports it, whether primary sources are available, and whether independent sources genuinely corroborate it. Demonstration: compare two conflicting claims and produce a short source trail that distinguishes primary evidence, reporting, opinion, and unsupported assertion.

nodes.title: Use numeracy, ratios, units, and estimation
nodes.description: Capability: calculate and sanity-check percentages, ratios, rates, unit conversions, orders of magnitude, and estimates used in everyday choices. Demonstration: estimate before calculating, show units and assumptions, then explain whether the result is plausible.

nodes.title: Interpret statistics, charts, and everyday risk
nodes.description: Capability: read axes and denominators, distinguish absolute from relative change, understand base rates and sample limitations, and avoid treating correlation as causation. Demonstration: explain a chart or risk statement in plain language, identify a plausible misleading interpretation, and state what extra information would change the conclusion.

nodes.title: Represent uncertainty and update beliefs proportionately
nodes.description: Capability: express confidence at a useful level of precision, separate confidence from importance, seek disconfirming evidence, and update a claim without pretending that uncertainty has disappeared. Demonstration: record a prediction with a reason and confidence level, list a possible disconfirmation, then explain a later update.

nodes.title: Reason scientifically about mechanisms and causes
nodes.description: Capability: formulate answerable questions, propose competing explanations, distinguish observation from intervention, make testable predictions, and describe limits of a result. Demonstration: design a small ethical, low-risk test with a comparison, a measurable outcome, and a stated alternative explanation; do not generalize beyond its evidence.

nodes.title: Recognize systems, feedback, stocks, and unintended effects
nodes.description: Capability: map components, flows, delays, constraints, feedback loops, and externalities in a real process. Demonstration: draw a small causal-loop or stock-and-flow sketch for a household, service, or community problem and identify a feedback loop plus one possible unintended consequence.

nodes.title: Make informed personal cash-flow and borrowing decisions
nodes.description: Capability: distinguish income, recurring and irregular costs, assets, liabilities, interest, fees, inflation, and emergency buffers. Demonstration: build a realistic monthly cash-flow example and compare two borrowing or saving scenarios using total cost, time, and explicit assumptions; this is education, not personalized financial advice.

nodes.title: Evaluate consumer offers, contracts, and fraud risks
nodes.description: Capability: compare total cost and exit conditions, identify pressure tactics and common fraud signals, protect identity documents, and know where to seek independent local consumer advice. Demonstration: review a fictional offer and identify missing terms, fees, risks, verification steps, and questions to ask before committing.

nodes.title: Protect accounts, devices, privacy, and consent
nodes.description: Capability: use unique passwords or a password manager, multifactor authentication where available, timely updates, recovery methods, backups, and deliberate sharing permissions; recognize and report suspicious requests. Demonstration: complete a non-invasive personal security checklist and explain how to recover one account without sharing secrets with an assessor.

nodes.title: Use AI systems critically and safely
nodes.description: Capability: identify when AI output is a hypothesis rather than a source, verify consequential claims against independent evidence, disclose meaningful assistance where required, and protect confidential data. For code or automation, test in a bounded environment and require human review before consequential actions. Demonstration: audit a deliberately flawed AI answer, trace two claims to sources, and describe what must not be delegated.

nodes.title: Navigate health information and care decisions
nodes.description: Capability: find relevant, current health information; distinguish general education from diagnosis; prepare clear questions for qualified professionals; compare stated benefits, risks, alternatives, and uncertainty; and recognize when local urgent or emergency services should be consulted. Demonstration: create a question list for a fictional appointment and trace a health claim to an appropriate authoritative source. This module does not diagnose or replace clinical care.

nodes.title: Understand civic institutions and participate with evidence
nodes.description: Capability: identify which local institution or process is responsible for an issue, distinguish law or official policy from commentary, compare arguments fairly, and find a legitimate participation or appeal route. Demonstration: trace a fictional public claim to the relevant primary document and map the responsible institution; legal details must be localized to the learner's jurisdiction.

nodes.title: Communicate clearly and work through disagreement
nodes.description: Capability: state goals and constraints, listen for the other person's model of the situation, distinguish impact from intent, ask clarifying questions, negotiate workable next steps, and record shared decisions. Demonstration: use a scenario to produce a neutral issue summary, at least two competing interpretations, a fair question, and an observable next action.

nodes.title: Design a self-directed learning loop
nodes.description: Capability: define a specific learning outcome, test prior knowledge, practice retrieving information without looking, space reviews over time, seek corrective feedback, and apply learning in a new context. Demonstration: create a short learning plan with a baseline task, practice schedule, retrieval prompts, feedback source, and delayed transfer check. Presentation preferences may be respected but do not by themselves prove a learning advantage.

nodes.title: Prepare for local emergencies and act within limits
nodes.description: Capability: locate official local alerts and emergency contacts, plan household communication and evacuation, prepare context-appropriate essential supplies, and recognize when to seek qualified help rather than improvise. Demonstration: complete a household or individual plan for one plausible hazard and walk through a scenario using official local guidance; first-aid skills require appropriate practical instruction.

nodes.title: Understand everyday energy, water, and material systems
nodes.description: Capability: identify major inputs, outputs, losses, maintenance needs, and environmental trade-offs in a household or community system. Demonstration: estimate one meaningful resource flow, state the measurement basis, and compare two interventions including cost, reliability, rebound effects, and who bears the impacts.

nodes.title: Plan, execute, and improve a useful project
nodes.description: Capability: translate a problem into a testable goal, define scope and acceptance criteria, identify dependencies and risks, make progress visible, test the result, and run a blameless after-action review. Demonstration: deliver a small artifact or service, show evidence against its acceptance criteria, and document one failed assumption and the resulting change.

nodes.title: Navigate work, collaboration, and career development
nodes.description: Capability: understand role expectations, deliverables, feedback, fair agreements, basic pay documentation, workplace safety, skill evidence, and how employment rules vary by jurisdiction. Demonstration: turn a fictional role description into an evidence-backed skills gap plan, work sample, questions about terms, and a next-step learning plan.

edges.rationale: Source assessment is clearer when observations, interpretations, and assumptions are separated.
Interpreting denominators, rates, and scale depends on basic numeracy.
Separating data from interpretation reduces overclaiming.
Numerical estimates can make uncertainty more explicit where quantification is useful.
Base rates and sample limitations support calibrated uncertainty.
Scientific inquiry depends on distinguishing observations from explanations.
Source evaluation helps judge background evidence.
Investigations require interpretable measures and data.
Predictions, alternatives, and updates strengthen test design.
System maps need quantitative attention to rates, stocks, and delays.
Models and alternative explanations support systems analysis.
Cash-flow, rates, and total-cost comparisons depend on numeracy.
Risk and rate literacy improve financial comparisons.
Consumer-offer comparison builds on understanding total cost and time.
Independent source checks help identify fraudulent or misleading offers.
Source verification is useful when handling suspicious digital requests.
Critical AI use depends on source and claim verification.
Privacy and access-control habits constrain safe use of AI tools.
Health-information navigation requires separating claim, evidence, and interpretation.
Health claims require careful source selection and provenance.
Basic risk and denominator literacy helps interpret health statistics.
Civic claims should be traced to primary documents and accountable institutions.
Resource trade-offs depend on flows, constraints, feedback, and externalities.
Resource comparisons depend on units and scale.
Distinguishing observation from interpretation can reduce avoidable conflict.
Workplace coordination depends on clear communication and shared expectations.
Understanding pay and cash flow helps formulate practical work-related questions.
Self-directed learning benefits from distinguishing current knowledge from assumption.
Confidence calibration helps learners decide what to review.
Emergency plans should rely on verified, locally authoritative information.
Preparedness improves when dependencies, bottlenecks, and cascading failures are considered.
Knowing local institutions helps locate official alerts and assistance.
Delivery plans improve when dependencies and feedback are visible.
Projects need clear handoffs, scope, and shared acceptance criteria.
Explicit assumptions and review points help projects adapt to new evidence.
Feedback and reflection support iterative project improvement.
Evidence-backed skill claims and agreement review require source discipline.

learning_paths.title: Reasoning Under Uncertainty
learning_paths.description: A compact foundation for checking claims, reading data, representing uncertainty, and doing testable investigations.

learning_paths.title: Sovereign Digital Participation
learning_paths.description: Protect accounts and data, evaluate AI output, and trace civic claims to accountable primary sources.

learning_paths.title: Personal Resilience and Agency
learning_paths.description: Build practical capability for financial choices, health-information navigation, local preparedness, work, and project delivery.

learning_paths.title: Self-Directed Lifelong Learning
learning_paths.description: Set a goal, calibrate current understanding, use evidence-informed practice, and test transfer in a useful project.

learning_paths.title: Understand and Improve Living Systems
learning_paths.description: Combine data, scientific inquiry, systems models, resource literacy, and iterative intervention.
